cues.en: So I just released a new notation font which consists of common symbols used in sheet music. It's available for free under the s I l open font license and will also be the new default in MuseScore,
cues.zh: 我最近发布了一款新的记谱字体，收录了乐谱中常用的符号。它基于 SIL 开源字体许可证免费提供，还将成为 MuseScore 的新默认字体，

cues.en: a free composition software used by over 5,000,000 people. The aim was to help improve the appearance of digitally produced notation,
cues.zh: 一款超过500万人使用的免费排谱软件。其初衷是帮助提升数字化乐谱的排版美观度，

cues.en: which still has some way to go before it can reach the standards of the hand engraved styles favored by publishers until around the nineteen nineties. But there have been some really great improvements and technical advances in digital notation over the last few years, and I couldn't resist the opportunity to help push that envelope a little bit further. Now making this font was a much tougher ride than I expected, and I didn't quite realize what I was letting myself in for. Once you begin to understand why certain aspects of notation are arranged the way they are, you become more sensitive to the intricacies and precision of the discipline, discovering a ton of hidden compromises that you never quite realized had been made, evolved through trial and error over the centuries. I learned a lot throughout the course of this project and I wanna share how fascinatingly
cues.zh:
它距离出版社直到 20 世纪 90 年代前后一直青睐的手工雕刻风格，还有一段距离。不过，过去几年里，数字乐谱记谱已经取得了非常出色的改进和技术进步，我实在无法抗拒这个机会，想把它再向前推进一点。

制作这款字体的过程比我预想中艰难得多，我一开始完全没意识到自己要面对什么。

当你开始理解记谱中的某些元素为什么要以特定方式排列时，你会更加关注这门学科的复杂性和精确性，也会发现大量自己从未意识到的隐性取舍，而这些取舍都是经过几个世纪的反复试错逐渐演变而来的。

在这个项目的整个过程中，我学到了很多，也想和大家分享这件事有多么令人着迷。

cues.en: nuanced, and also nightmarishly tedious, the experience was. And in the spirit of pain homage to those who laid the groundwork that we're building upon today, this video also about the main inspiration for our new notation style, the now sadly abandoned program Score and its creator Leland Smith. A man with enormous talent, perseverance, dedication.
cues.zh: 这段经历既微妙复杂，又繁琐得如同噩梦。本着痛苦致敬的精神，向那些为我们今天所构建之物打下基础的人致敬，本视频还讲述我们新记谱风格的主要灵感来源——如今令人遗憾地被弃置的程序 Score，以及它的创造者 Leland Smith。一个拥有巨大才华、毅力和奉献精神的人。

cues.en: So for those who don't know, I took over as MuseScore's head of design last year and became its product owner in July 2020. And I must admit that creating a notation font was not really on my short list of things to do when I started because there were so many other issues I wanted to address first. But this changed when I met the professional engraver, Simon Smith, who had heard that I was interested in doing a video about score and got in contact to offer to demo it for me. Now before I go any further, I need to address a slightly awkward problem for this story. You see, Simon, who is the co creator of this font, is also a big fan of this thing called
cues.zh:
所以，可能有人还不知道，去年我接任了 MuseScore 的设计负责人，并于 2020 年 7 月成为产品负责人。

我得承认，刚开始时，制作一款乐谱字体并不在我的优先事项清单上，因为还有很多其他问题等着我先处理。

但后来我遇到了专业制谱师 Simon Smith，情况就变了。他听说我有兴趣做一段关于乐谱的视频，便联系我，提出可以为我演示。

继续讲下去之前，我得先说说这个故事里一个有点尴尬的问题。

Simon 是这款字体的共同创作者，同时也是这个叫……的东西的忠实粉丝。

cues.en: privacy and would prefer not to appear in this video. And you know, that's his right. He could, you know, if he doesn't want to, then it's fine. But since it's kinda hard to describe a collaboration between two people in video essay format when one of them can't be seen, I'm gonna have to think outside the box a bit here. So let's represent Simon with this drawing.
cues.zh: 他很注重隐私，也不太想出现在这段视频里。你知道，这是他的权利。他要是不愿意，那也没关系。不过，在视频随笔这种形式里，要讲清楚两个人的合作，却有一个人不能露面，确实有点难，所以我得稍微跳出框框想想办法。那我们就用这幅画来代表 Simon 吧。

cues.en: Let's take it for a test run. Hi, Simon.
cues.zh: 我们先试运行一下。你好，Simon。

cues.en: Perfect. Let's move on. Simon worked at the publishing house Boozy and Hawks and over his career has worked with composers like Harrison Burtwistle, Henrik Goretzky, and Karl Leinz Stockhausen.
cues.zh: 太好了，我们继续。Simon 曾在出版商 Boosey & Hawkes 工作，职业生涯中与 Harrison Birtwistle、Henryk Górecki 和 Karlheinz Stockhausen 等作曲家合作过。

cues.en: And in all cases, his app of choice has always been Score. And he's not alone. Many engravers working for the biggest publishers, Boozy and Hawks, Schott, Universal Edition, Peters, Schirmer, Brightcove, Anson, etcetera, still use it today. But here's the thing. Score hasn't been commercially available since 2013
cues.zh: 在所有情况下，他选择的应用一直都是 Score。他并不孤单。如今，许多为大型出版商工作的制谱师仍在使用它，比如 Boosey & Hawkes、Schott、Universal Edition、Peters、Schirmer、Brightcove、Anson 等等。但问题是，Score 自 2013 年起就已停止商业销售，

cues.en: and it is literally impossible to buy a legal copy of it anymore. So how can an app that's widely used at the highest levels of the industry become abandonware?
cues.zh: 如今已经根本买不到合法版本了。那么，一款在业界顶尖领域广泛使用的应用，怎么会沦为弃用软件呢？

cues.en: And what's this got to do with our notation font?
cues.zh: 这又和我们的记谱字体有什么关系？

cues.en: Well, that's that's that's what's coming up. Coming up now.
cues.zh: 好，这些内容马上就会揭晓。接下来就讲。

cues.en: So Score was a notation app created by the composer and Stanford professor Leland Smith who evolved it on various computer systems throughout seventies while at the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory. He eventually released it commercially in 1987.
cues.zh: Score 是一款记谱应用，由作曲家、斯坦福大学教授 Leland Smith 开发。他在 70 年代任职于斯坦福人工智能实验室期间，陆续将它移植到不同的计算机系统上，最终于 1987 年将其商业化发布。

cues.en: It was written in the Fortran programming language and ran on MS DOS. Since its purpose was not for composing, but for laying out and printing sheet music, it ran very differently to the way apps work today. Instead of a point and click interface, users had to type out multiple strings of code to define information that should appear on the score. Let me quickly describe this. To begin, you needed to gradually define different aspects of notation in separate passes. There were five passes in total. In the first, you defined a few essentials. Here you can see the letters t and r, which mean treble clef, followed by k three f, meaning key signature three flats. And then you can see four four, which defines the time signature.
cues.zh: 它用 Fortran 编程语言编写，运行在 MS-DOS 上。它的用途不是作曲，而是排版和打印乐谱，所以运行方式和今天的应用截然不同。用户不能通过点击操作，而是要输入多行代码，来定义乐谱上要显示的内容。我来快速介绍一下。首先，你需要分多个步骤逐步定义记谱的各个方面，总共分为五步。第一步定义一些基本信息。这里可以看到字母 t 和 r，表示高音谱号，后面是 k 3 f，表示三个降号的调号。然后是 4 4，表示拍号。

cues.en: Next, typed out a row of pitches and rests along with the direction of the stems. And if we look down here, you'll notice that nothing has appeared yet. That's because you needed to finish typing out each pass before committing it, and only then would you see a visual result. Now with the second pass, and I found this really weird when I first saw it, you then went back over the pitches you just entered and only then assigned durations to them. Then over the course of the next three passes, you got the opportunity to define all the possible parameters for that line of music. And then once done, you could move on. In this case, to the lower voice on the same stave. So as you can probably see, score was not built to be something that you could just pick up and intuitively use. Not only does the input method take some getting used to, users also needed to come to terms with a myriad of tables which contained codes for every conceivable symbol or action. In addition, score didn't make many decisions for you. It had no concept of instruments. It didn't make your score look pretty by default, so required a lot of manual adjustment. It didn't auto generate part scores for you. It basically gave you a staff and after that you were on your own. This is the antithesis of how modern applications are designed today, which is understandable considering that it was released in the nineteen eighties. But on the other hand, because it was essentially a sandbox, there were no limitations to what kind of score you could create with it. Once you overcame the steep learning curve, you could produce scores extremely quickly. Trust me, Simon can lay out music and score faster than anyone else I've seen in any other program. This is why the app has so many die hard advocates even to this day. I really like how Score simplifies the notation on the screen. This is to get around the limitations of the hardware it was built to run on, which could only display 31,000 vectors at a time. But as basic as this interface looks, Score's superpower was the quality of its output. Leland Smith was highly attentive to the art of beautiful engraving and wanted Score to be able to produce sheet music of such high quality that it could replace the manual systems that engravers were using, which were unbelievably time consuming. The prevalent method at that point was called the Notaset system, where engravers would transfer notes onto paper using a spatula. Another method used sheets of metal where you had to mark up each sheet before painstakingly hammering symbols onto it, followed by hours spent carefully etching stems, slurs, and beams. In order to get score to produce sheet music of sufficiently high quality, Leland spent years consulting the largest publishers for advice, gradually improving its feature set until it was flexible enough to handle their needs, while refining the hundreds of common symbols that would be needed. This latter task can't have been easy given the very basic nature of vector drawing tools in the seventies. Back then, vectors could only consist of straight lines, so creating hundreds of complex symbols in score must have required superhuman patience. Around 1990, the publisher, Shot, provided Leland with proof sheets of their own notation symbols which were of a far higher quality than those SCOR had used previously. The work of adding this library to SCOR was handled by Leland's daughter, Stephanie, who had to blow up each symbol in size, project them on a grid, and plot the key points around them. This provided coordinates that could then be entered into an application Leland had developed called draw, which in turn produced basic vector versions of each symbol. Considering the multiple hundreds of symbols involved, this is an amazing achievement and a testament to single-minded drive to achieve the highest possible quality. Which is one of the reasons why myself and Simon were inspired to work on our own pet project. And with that in mind, let's now leave Score for a moment and fast forward to the present day to begin looking at what we've done.
cues.zh: 接下来，输入一行音高和休止符，以及符干的方向。往下看，你会发现目前还什么都没显示。这是因为每一步都要全部输入完再提交，提交后才能看到图形结果。到了第二步，你要回头给刚才输入的音符指定时值。我第一次看到时觉得特别奇怪。接下来的三步里，你可以为这行音乐定义所有可能的参数。完成后，就可以继续处理同一谱表上的低声部了。你们大概也看出来了，Score 并不是那种拿起来就能直观上手的应用。输入方式需要时间适应，用户还得熟悉一大堆代码表，里面列出了各种符号和操作对应的代码。此外，Score 不会替你做太多决定。它没有乐器的概念，也不会默认把乐谱排得很漂亮，因此需要大量手动调整。它也不会自动生成分谱。它基本上只给你一条谱表，之后就得靠自己。这和现代应用的设计理念正好相反。当然，考虑到它发布于 80 年代，这也可以理解。但另一方面，它本质上是个沙盒，你想做什么样的乐谱都没有限制。克服陡峭的学习曲线后，你就能极快地排谱。相信我，我见过 Simon 用 Score 排谱，比任何人用其他程序都快。这也是这款应用至今仍有这么多死忠用户的原因。我很喜欢 Score 在屏幕上简化记谱的方式。这是为了适应它所运行的硬件限制，当时的硬件每次只能显示 31,000 个矢量。虽然界面看起来很简陋，但 Score 的真正强项是输出质量。Leland Smith 非常注重雕版艺术之美，希望 Score 能制作出足以取代人工制谱的高质量乐谱，而当时的人工制谱耗时惊人。那时最常见的方法叫作 Notaset 系统，制谱师用刮刀把音符转印到纸上。另一种方法是用金属板，先在每块板上做好标记，再一点点把符号敲上去，之后还要花数小时仔细刻出符干、连线和符杠。为了让 Score 输出足够高质量的乐谱，Leland 花了多年时间向大型出版商征求意见，逐步改进功能，直到它足以灵活满足他们的需求，同时还不断完善数百种常用符号。考虑到 70 年代的矢量绘图工具非常基础，这项工作肯定不容易。当时矢量图只能由直线组成，所以在 Score 里绘制数百种复杂符号，想必需要超乎常人的耐心。大约在 1990 年，出版商 Schott 把自家质量远胜于 Score 原有符号的记谱符号样张交给了 Leland。将这套符号库加入 Score 的工作由 Leland 的女儿 Stephanie 完成。她得先放大每个符号，投影到网格上，再标出关键点，由此得到的坐标再输入 Leland 开发的一款名为 draw 的应用中，最终生成每个符号的基础矢量版本。需要处理数百种符号，这项成就令人惊叹，也体现了他们一心追求最高品质的执着。这也是我和 Simon 受到启发、开始做自己的业余项目的原因之一。说到这里，我们先暂时放下 Score，把时间快进到今天，来看看我们做出的成果。

cues.en: Today, unlike Score, modern applications use font files to store notation. This is useful not only because they can be swapped with other fonts and shared between applications, but also because they store a lot of detailed spatial information too. When setting out to create our font, Simon and I agreed on a few goals. First, we wanted the notation style to function as the new default in MuseScore.
cues.zh: 如今与 Score 不同，现代应用使用字体文件来存储乐谱符号。这不仅便于替换其他字体并在应用间共享，而且还能存储大量的精细空间信息。在着手设计我们的字体时，我和 Simon 确立了几个目标。首先，我们希望这种记谱风格能成为 MuseScore 的全新默认样式。

cues.en: So our focus was on creating a highly finessed version of the classic notation style. Second, we particularly wanted to match the feeling of precision and balance that score had so successfully achieved. Third, since legibility is of the utmost importance, we wanted to avoid the impulse to make something really flashy that draws attention to itself. In a way, we wanted to make the Helvetica of music notation with everything feeling just right so performing musicians almost don't know it's there. The first thing to determine was weight. We definitely wanted to avoid the trap of making it overly thin, which is a bit of a tendency in digital notation over the last twenty years with the results often feeling a little insubstantial.
cues.zh: 因此我们的重点是打造经典记谱风格的极致精修版。其次，我们特别希望能达到 Score 所成功呈现的那种精准与平衡感。第三，鉴于易读性至关重要，我们想克制住做过于炫目、吸睛设计的冲动。从某种意义上说，我们想打造音乐记谱界的 Helvetica，一切都恰到好处，让演奏者几乎察觉不到它的存在。首先要确定的是字重。我们坚决避免陷入做得过细的陷阱，这是过去二十年数字记谱的一种倾向，往往让人觉得有些单薄。

cues.en: The next thing to figure out was how to make our font as available to as many people as possible. Historically, there's been very little coordination between applications which all created their own bespoke systems. Meaning that a font used in one usually couldn't be used in another without a ton of specialized modifications. That is until the creation of the standard music font layout or SMUFL project in 2013
cues.zh: 接下来要想清楚的是，如何让尽可能多的人用上我们的字体。历史上，各应用之间几乎没有协同，全都在自建定制系统。这意味着某个应用里的字体，若不经过大量专门修改，通常无法用于另一个。直到 2013 年标准音乐字体布局（即 SMuFL 项目）的诞生，

cues.en: led by Daniel Spreadbury who also manages the notation app Dorico. The goal of SMUFL is to provide a much needed classification system which now covers thousands of symbols representing a range of different styles of music from all over the world.
cues.zh: 该项目由 Daniel Spreadbury 主导，他也是乐谱应用 Dorico 的负责人。SMuFL 的目标是提供一套亟需的分类系统，目前已涵盖数千个符号，代表着来自世界各地的多种不同音乐风格。

cues.en: Now, since I have a background in both typography and iconography,
cues.zh: 由于我兼有排印学和图标设计的背景，

cues.en: the task of drawing and refining the symbols fell to me. Simon's role was to define the spatial relationships and the special characteristics for each symbol, along with the accompanying style settings for every other aspect of the sheet music's appearance. But for me, Simon was even more crucial as a second set of eyes. Someone who could point out little areas where revisions were needed, which he did.
cues.zh: 绘制和打磨符号的任务便落在了我身上。Simon 的职责则是定义每个符号的空间关系和专属特征，以及乐谱外观其他方方面面的配套样式设置。但对我来说，Simon 更关键的作用是充当第二双眼睛——一个能指出需要修改的细微之处的人，而他也确实做到了。

cues.en: Never endingly. And at times, it really felt like he was less a colleague and more an artistic personal trainer, constantly pushing me to go back and do another revision.
cues.zh: 而且是无休无止地提。有时真觉得他不像同事，反倒像个艺术私教，不断催着我回头再改一版。

cues.en: Go back and do another revision.
cues.zh: “回去再改一版。”

cues.en: Give me 10 reps on those mordants and we'll call it a day. And this back and forth really helps to further my appreciation of the pinpoint attention to detail you need to have to produce beautiful sheet music. And from here on out, some of you may need to keep your eyes peeled because we're about to enter into super subtle territory.
cues.zh: “把那些波音再改个 10 遍，今天就到这。”这种来回打磨真的让我进一步体会到，想要制作出精美的乐谱，需要何等精确入微的专注。从现在开始，大家可能得瞪大眼睛了，因为我们要进入超级精细的微观领域了。

cues.en: So let's start by looking at the first symbol I worked on, the treble clef, and how, initially, my iconographer's eye worked against me. I started by grabbing a few different examples that I liked, observing where I thought they worked and where they didn't. If we focus on the original symbol from score, bearing in mind that it looks a bit jagged up close, I'll show you the kinds of things that I wanted to alter. Starting with overall balance, this section seemed to me to be stooping forward slightly, a little beyond its central axis. And then looking down here, I noticed a slightly unpleasant variation in this curve, which starts off closer together, widens out a bit here, and then narrows again here. I also felt that this section was a little fat and it bugged me that the stem wasn't perfectly centered between these two points. I also felt the stem could do with a bit of thickening up too. So here's my first attempt to address all these things. And on first sight, you might think that this looks okay. But no. It's actually a malformed atrocity. You see, it's all well and good for me to look at a few curves and lines and make a bunch of isolated corrections divorced from context. But when I place this on a staff alongside other symbols, it becomes obvious that the changes I made weren't really helping anything at all. If we look again at the original score symbol, the difference is pretty obvious. This treble clef feels grounded and well positioned alongside the other symbols, whereas Damien here looks unbalanced as if recoiling from this key signature or wistfully glancing up at the moon. All my alterations to the stroke, reducing the heavier parts and bulking up the stem, only seemed to actually reduce its distinctiveness, which I discovered later made it feel less consistent with the rest of the family. There were two big lessons in this. The first is that changes which look good in isolation may end up looking pretty dismal in context.
cues.zh:
那么，我们先来看我着手设计的第一个符号：高音谱号，以及最初我那套图标设计眼光是怎么拖了后腿的。我先找了几个自己喜欢的不同版本，观察它们哪些地方好，哪些地方不好。我们聚焦在 Score 的原始符号上，近看会发现它有些锯齿。我来讲讲自己想调整的地方。先看整体平衡，我觉得这一段稍微有点前倾，偏离了中轴线。再看下面这儿，我注意到这段曲线变化得不太舒服：一开始两边靠得比较近，到这里稍微变宽，然后在这里又收窄。我还觉得这一段有点粗，而且谱干没有正好位于这两个点的中间。我也觉得谱干可以再加粗一点。这是我第一次尝试解决这些问题。乍一看，你可能觉得还不错。但其实不然。这简直是个畸形的怪物。你看，单独看几条曲线和线条，脱离上下文做一堆零散修改，当然没问题。可一旦把它放到五线谱上，和其他符号摆在一起，就会发现这些改动其实一点忙都没帮上。再看一眼 Score 的原始符号，差别显而易见。这个高音谱号和其他符号放在一起，显得稳当、位置恰当；而这里的 Damien 却失去了平衡，仿佛正躲避这个调号，或是惆怅地仰望月亮。我对笔画做的所有调整，比如减细较粗的部分、加粗谱干，结果似乎只是削弱了它的辨识度。后来我发现，这也让它和其他同系列符号显得不够一致。

这里有两个重要的教训。第一，单独看起来不错的改动，放到实际场景里可能就不怎么样了。

cues.en: The second lesson is more subtle, That good engraving is really all about contrast.
cues.zh: 第二个教训更微妙：好的制谱，关键在于对比。

cues.en: In this case between the pick and pin lines of the treble clef. But in other ways too as you'll see in my next example. Anyway, after doing multiple revisions, receiving voluminous reports from Simon It's not good. And posting updates of my progress on Twitter, which produced some really eagle eyed observations, by the way. My original symbol went from this to this. And I hope it's obvious to you how much better this symbol fits in with its surroundings. This thinner stem feels more consistent with both the staff lines and these accidental stems, which in combination contrasts really nicely with the bit that I thought was too fat. And if we zoom out, can see that this gives the cleft more presence. It's good to keep thinner lines similarly thin so that the thicker strokes stand out more. If there's a lot of variation in stroke thickness, then the contrast is less effective. Now, we compare my cleft with the original score version, you can see some obvious differences. But this time, I matched the feel of the symbol while making all kinds of refinements to the curves that are now possible given the precision of the tools available today. However, there were many places where we deviated from score much more noticeably. For example, Simon and I both felt that the original sharp and natural accidentals were just much too small. Also just wasn't a fan of the score for MATA at all and designed ours to feel more like a natural part of the family. And see if you can spot the differences between these flat accidentals. We agonized over this. I'm serious. Apart from that, the SMuFL classification calls for hundreds of symbols that were never added to score. For example, these microtonal symbols. Yeah. These might look easy, but trust me it took forever to get that arrow to look good when intersecting those staff lines. But for me, the toughest thing to design were without a doubt the note flags. Let me show you why. If we start with my first version this eighth note looks okay. For the sixteenth note though it's good practice to maintain the stem height which requires me to redraw these two strokes in a way that then pushes the tail down below that of the eighth note, which causes it to terminate right at the bar line. I'll describe why we didn't like that in a second. Now if you then add another stroke for a thirty second note, it makes logical sense to increase the stem height by one staff space. That's the distance between these two lines, which maintains a nice visual symmetry, which you continue for sixty fourth and a hundred and twenty eighth notes for those people who are into that. But there are three issues with doing this. The first is that these gaps are just too big and when read at normal sizes can look a bit weird. You can thicken up the stroke to combat this, but then they look too flabby. The second issue is that the notation can end up becoming too tall, pushing other symbols upwards and cramping the space between staves. Third, remember what I said earlier about the importance of contrast? Well, this is a classic example. You see, these horizontal staff lines provide more than just a reference that helps us understand pitch. They also provide a stable visual reference that helps the other elements stand out to catch our eye. In the case of this flag, it's a bad idea to allow it to terminate right on the line here. A musician reading at a fast pace will able to discern the symbol more clearly if this is moved up a little bit to reveal the edge. You might think that the obvious solution is to terminate the flag at the halfway point. But that's a problem too because if the note moves up one pitch, which is a shift of exactly half a stave space, it ends up terminating right at the line again. So even though the symmetry satisfied my OCD, I needed to make a few compromises.
cues.zh:
在这个例子里，指的是高音谱号弯钩与谱干线条之间的对比。其他方面也一样，下一例你就会看到。总之，经过多轮修改，收到了 Simon 大量的反馈——“不行”——还在 Twitter 上发布了进度，得到了一些观察力特别敏锐的意见。顺带一提，我的原始符号就这样从这个改成了这个。希望你能看出，新符号和周围的元素搭配得好得多。较细的谱干和五线谱线条、这些变音记号的谱干更一致，同时也和我觉得过粗的部分形成了很好的对比。缩小来看，这让谱号更醒目。较细的线条最好保持同样纤细，这样较粗的笔画才更突出。如果笔画粗细变化太多，对比效果就会减弱。

现在把我的谱号和 Score 的原版放在一起比较，可以看到一些明显差异。但这次，我保留了符号原有的感觉，同时利用现代工具的精度，对曲线做了各种细化。不过，有不少地方我们和 Score 的差异要明显得多。比如，Simon 和我都觉得原版的升号和还原号实在太小了。我也完全不喜欢 Score 的 MATA 字体，所以我们重新设计了一套，让它更像整个符号家族的自然一员。看看你能不能找出这些降号之间的差异。我们为此反复纠结了很久，真的。除此之外，SMuFL 的分类还要求加入数百个 Score 从未收录的符号，比如这些微分音符号。是的，它们看起来简单，但相信我，要让箭头穿过五线谱线时看起来协调，花了我很长时间。

不过，对我来说最难设计的绝对是音符旗。让我解释一下原因。从我的第一个版本开始看，这个八分音符看起来还不错。但到了十六分音符，通常需要保持谱干高度，这就得重新画这两笔，结果尾部会低于八分音符的尾部，最后正好落在小节线上。为什么我们不喜欢这样，我稍后再说。再加一笔变成三十二分音符时，按逻辑应该把谱干高度增加一个谱间距，也就是这两条线之间的距离，这样视觉上就能保持良好的对称性。对于六十四分音符和一百二十八分音符也可以照此类推，适合有这种需求的人。

但这样做有三个问题。第一，这些间距实在太大，在正常大小下看起来会有点怪。加粗笔画可以缓解这个问题，但那样看起来又会太臃肿。第二，记谱可能会变得太高，把其他符号往上挤，也让五线谱之间的空间变得拥挤。第三，还记得我之前说过对比的重要性吗？这就是个典型例子。五线谱的横线不只是帮助我们理解音高的参照，也提供了稳定的视觉参照，让其他元素更醒目，能吸引我们的注意。对于这个音符旗，让它正好终止在线上可不是好主意。快速读谱的演奏者会更容易看清这个符号，只要把它稍微往上移，露出边缘。你可能觉得显而易见的解决办法，是让音符旗终止在两条线的正中间。但这也有问题，因为音符升高一个音级，也就是恰好移动半个谱间距后，它又会正好终止在线上。所以，虽然这种对称性很合我的强迫症胃口，我还是得做些妥协。

cues.en: Anyway, after three quite tough revisions,
cues.zh: 好，经过三次相当艰难的修改之后，

cues.en: here was where I landed. The flags were shorter but still managed to look nice against the staff lines. And you can see here that they're all terminating at the three quarter staff position apart from the eighth note, which terminates at the one quarter staff position.
cues.zh: 我最终定稿的是这个。符尾更短了，但放在谱线上看起来依然很漂亮。你可以看到，除了八分音符结束在五线的四分之一位置，其余的都结束在四分之三位置。

cues.en: This ensures that the flag endings never terminate on a staff line.
cues.zh: 这样能保证符尾的末端永远不会落在谱线上。

cues.en: Success.
cues.zh: 成功了。

cues.en: Oh, actually, no. These weren't good either. You see, that was when we realized that we'd forgotten to test them with tremolo marks, which it turned out intersected nastily with this inner arc.
cues.zh: 哦，其实不然。这些也不行。因为那时我们意识到，我们忘了拿震音记号来测试，结果发现震音记号会和内侧的弧线交叉得很不美观。

cues.en: In addition, Simon then went and made the one comment I was dreading. It's not nice. Meaning, wouldn't it be great if all the flags terminated at the same position? Which once he'd said it, nagged at me until I finally got around to revising them for a fifth time. You can see now that all the flags are lining up. And in particular, I'm quite proud of how the eighth note and the tremolo look together. But, you know, even as I'm saying this, I'm almost certain that I'll have to do a sixth and probably a seventh revision before the next version of the font is released. Oh, and that's another point actually. This is only version one. We'll need to collect a lot of user feedback and add hundreds more symbols before we'll be even close to done.
cues.zh: 此外，Simon 还说了一句我最怕听到的评论。不好听。意思是，如果所有符尾都终止在同一个位置岂不是更好？这话一旦说出，就一直在我脑子里挥之不去，直到我终于着手第五次修改。现在你可以看到所有符尾都对齐了。特别是八分音符和震音的组合效果，我相当自豪。不过话说回来，就在我说这些的同时，我几乎可以肯定，在字体下一个版本发布之前，我还得做第六次、甚至很可能第七次修改。哦，对了，还有一点。这才只是第一个版本。我们还需要收集大量用户反馈、增加数百个新符号，才算接近完成。

cues.en: Probably the single biggest improvement we made to our notation font was to find a typeface that would complement it. The previous MuseScore default was called free serif, which was a Times New Roman clone. And we felt this was long due an upgrade. Ideally, we wanted to find something like New Century Schoolbook, which is still the preferred typeface at Boozy and Hawkes. And after a bit of searching, we found an open source version of New Century Schoolbook, which works extremely well due to its clarity, spacing, and straight serifs.
cues.zh: 我们对这款记谱字体做的最大一项改进，也许是找到了一款与之相配的正文字体。MuseScore 之前的默认字体叫 free serif，是 Times New Roman 的克隆版，我们觉得它早就该升级了。理想情况下，我们想找类似 New Century Schoolbook 的字体，它至今仍是 Boozy and Hawkes 出版社的首选字体。经过一番搜寻，我们找到了一个 New Century Schoolbook 的开源版本，它清晰度高、间距合理、衬线笔直，效果非常好。

cues.en: Since it uses the same GPL license as MuseScore, we were able to make alterations to it and package it as our own default typeface. Open source software can just be so great to work with sometimes. Anyway, we renamed this variant Edwin, named after Edwin Ginn, the American philanthropist who originally commissioned New Century Schoolbook. He's another very interesting and inspirational person who, like Leland Smith, is worth reading up about. And speaking of Leland Smith, let's return back to the story of Score.
cues.zh: 由于它和 MuseScore 同样使用 GPL 许可证，我们可以对它进行修改，并打包成我们自己的默认字体。开源软件有时候就是这么好用。总之，我们把这个变体命名为 Edwin，得名于 Edwin Ginn——这位美国慈善家当年出资委托设计了 New Century Schoolbook。他和 Leland Smith 一样，是另一位非常有趣、令人敬佩的人物，值得去了解一下。说到 Leland Smith，我们回到 Score 的故事吧。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: after the success of Score four, Leland set about creating a new version called WinScore,
cues.zh: 在 Score 四大获成功之后，Leland 着手开发一个叫 WinScore 的新版本，

cues.en: which was to run on Windows rather than DOS. It would have a more advanced interface as well as a greater memory capacity to overcome the vector limit problem I described earlier. Unusually though, after the release of WinScore, as a way of speeding up its adoption, Leland made the decision to withdraw all previous versions of Score from the market which made them impossible to buy anymore. However, WinScore was still a beta product and suffered from a few serious stability issues. And most users preferred to stick with the DOS version until these problems were addressed. However, before this could happen, on the 12/17/2013,
cues.zh: 它要运行在 Windows 上而不是 DOS。它会拥有更先进的界面以及更大的内存容量，来解决我之前提到的向量数上限问题。但不同寻常的是，在发布 WinScore 之后，为了加快它的普及，Leland 决定将之前所有版本的 Score 全部退市，让它们再也买不到。然而，WinScore 当时还是个测试版产品，存在几个严重的稳定性问题。大多数用户宁愿继续用 DOS 版，等这些问题解决。可是没等到那一天，2013年12月17日，

cues.en: Leland Smith sadly passed away at the age of 88.
cues.zh: Leland Smith 不幸离世，享年 88 岁。

cues.en: What caused the users of Score even more anguish is that he left no arrangements in place that would allow the project to be continued by anyone else, despite having been asked by his colleagues on numerous occasions to do so. After his death, attempts were made to convince his surviving family to grant permission to continue the project which were apparently ignored. Listen to a summary of this on the support site's score box which is quite telling. His heirs have made no comment whatsoever as to the plans for the future maintenance or development of the program. This nonchalant attitude sadly perpetuates the curious unwillingness of Leland Smith to engage in reasonable discussions to ensure the ongoing maintenance and development of his software suite. Yet despite the obvious affection and commitment of his loyal user base, he failed to offer any kind of statement despite the consternation this caused among many loyal users and the outright hostility it eventually elicited from others. As a result of this, both score and win score sadly became abandonware
cues.zh: 让 Score 的用户更感痛苦的是，尽管同事们多次恳求，他却没有留下任何安排让其他人能接手这个项目。在他去世后，人们曾试图说服他的遗属授权继续推进该项目，但显然被置之不理。支持网站 score box 上的一段总结很能说明问题：“对于该程序未来的维护或开发计划，他的继承人未发表任何评论。这种漠不关心的态度，遗憾地延续了 Leland Smith 生前那种古怪的做法——拒绝就软件套件的持续维护与开发进行理性沟通。尽管忠实用户群体对他充满了热爱与支持，但他始终没有任何表态，这不仅让许多忠实用户感到惊愕，最终甚至引发了一些人的公开敌意。”正因如此，Score 和 WinScore 遗憾地沦为了“被遗弃的软件”。

cues.en: and the website registrations have since lapsed.
cues.zh: 相关的网站域名此后也已过期失效。

cues.en: It's not possible to know what Leland Smith's intentions really were here. Whether this result was the consequence of a deliberate decision or an unfortunate mixture of procrastination and oversight. One perspective provided by his colleague Thomas Broadhead was, he resisted all offers from others to help him with it. He perhaps feared that if others became involved professionally,
cues.zh: 我们无从知晓 Leland Smith 当时的真实意图究竟是什么，这一切究竟是他深思熟虑后的决定，还是拖延与疏忽交织出的不幸结果。他的同事 Thomas Broadhead 提供了一种视角：“他拒绝了所有人伸出的援手。他或许是担心，一旦有其他专业人士介入，

cues.en: the goals and philosophy of the program might be redirected in a different direction than he had intended.
cues.zh: 这个程序的目标和理念就会偏离他的初衷。”

cues.en: Make of that what you will. Regardless,
cues.zh: 至于怎么理解，见仁见智。但不管怎样，

cues.en: as I mentioned earlier, it's a testament to his unique talent that score is still used by engravers working for many of the biggest publishers today. It is however being gradually replaced over the years as new engravers joined the industry and its memory and that of its creator Leland Smith continues to fade.
cues.zh: 正如我之前提到的，时至今日，许多顶级出版机构的乐谱排版师仍在使用 Score，这本身就证明了他非凡的才华。不过这些年来，随着新一代排版师的加入，它正逐渐被取代，关于它以及它的创造者 Leland Smith 的记忆也在不断消逝。

cues.en: Speaking for myself, having become intimately acquainted with the output of Score, and Simon, who's worked with it for twenty years, we felt it was only fitting to offer some kind of tribute to its creator, to maintain his memory and honor his contribution to modern notation. So for that reason, it only felt right to name our new font Leland.
cues.zh: 就我个人而言，在深入了解了 Score 的输出效果之后，加上与它打了二十年交道的 Simon，我们都觉得，必须以某种方式向这位创造者致敬，铭记他的精神，并致敬他对现代乐谱排版做出的贡献。正因如此，我们将这款新字体命名为 Leland，再合适不过了。

cues.en: And as I mentioned earlier, it's free to use and should soon be supported by most notation applications out there. It's also going to be part of the new flagship style for MuseScore, which will feature lots of other engraving improvements too. You'll find relevant links in the description. And for those wondering why the interface hasn't updated along with the notation style given how much grief I gave it in a previous video, don't worry. That's coming next year. And I should probably also mention that although my characterization of Simon might seem perhaps a little unflattering,
cues.zh: 而且就像我之前说的，它是完全免费的，应该很快就会被市面上大多数记谱软件支持。它还会作为 MuseScore 全新旗舰样式的一部分，同时带来许多其他的乐谱排版改进。相关链接可以在简介中找到。可能有人会纳闷，鉴于我上一期视频把界面吐槽得那么狠，怎么这次界面没跟着记谱样式一起更新？别担心，明年就来。顺便提一句，虽然我对 Simon 的描写可能看起来有点不留情面，

cues.en: it's not. This is exactly what he's like. Have you got anything to say to the people before they go home, Simon? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah.
cues.zh: 但真没有，他平时就是这个样子的。在大家划走之前，Simon，你还有什么想对大家说的吗？行了。行了。行了。行了。行了。

cues.en: Hello.
cues.zh: 你好。

cues.en: If you like my diatribe,
cues.zh: 如果你喜欢我的这番吐槽，

cues.en: subscribe.
cues.zh: 欢迎订阅。
